Combined with RAG, it empowers models to: Think step-by-step Call tools, like a retriever or calculator Incorporate retrieved knowledge mid-thought How It Works in RAG: The LLM receives a prompt with a question and an action interface (e.g , "Search" "Lookup"): The LLM decides whether to retrieve, based on reasoning: Retrieved docs are fed back into the prompt mid-chain. The LLM generates a final answer grounded in external evidence_ Often implemented using LangChain's AgentExecutor with a retriever tool. When to Use: When queries require tool-use decision-making For complex or multi-hop queries (e.g , reasoning across multiple facts) When it's unclear whether external retrieval is needed Real-World Use Cases: Financial analyst assistant: Which insulin companies dropped prices and by how much?" Scientific assistant: "Summarize Crohn's treatments introduced in 2023. Legal bot: 'Was there a new law about insulin pricing last year?" Zvi Benami Multi-vector Retrieval What It Is: A technique where each document or passage is represented by multiple dense vectors, capturing different semantic aspects or subcomponents (e.g , title, body; metadata): This improves retrieval recall and relevance, especially for complex or multi-faceted queries. How It Works in RAG: Each document is split into logical parts (e.g,, title, paragraph, summary): Each part is embedded separately into its own vector During retrieval, the query is matched against all vectors, and top-scoring matches are used to reconstruct document context. Typically used with vector stores that support multi-field retrieval or hybrid indexes: When to Use: When documents have multiple relevant fields (e.g-, FAQ title + answer) When retrieval needs to match varied query phrasings For complex document types (e.g , reports, EHRs, scientific papers) Real-World Use Cases: Health: Matching diagnosis queries against symptoms + clinical notes Customer support: Matching How do refund?" against title + body of help articles Enterprise search: Searching based on document metadata + full content Latency Impact: Slightly higher more embeddings per document to search over: Cost: Higher upfront (indexing), but manageable at inference. Avoid When: Corpus is simple or short-form (e.g-, short notes) Storage space is limited (index size grows with multi-vectoring). 27 enana Inhenmraun Ueuu Ar/= ~duIa
